title: SEO content brief
footer_left: SEO content brief template by Angel Phommachan

blocks.title: Target audience and goal
fields: Target audience
Who the post is for and what they already know. Specific enough to picture.
Marketers starting out who write their own blog posts
Funnel stage
Where they are: just learning (awareness), comparing options (consideration), or ready to act (decision).
Awareness
☐ Awareness     ☐ Consideration     ☐ Decision
Content goal
What the post should do for the reader, and for you (traffic, trust, sign-ups, sales).
Readers can write a brief; I earn template downloads

blocks.title: Keyword research
blocks.hint: Free tools work: the Ahrefs Keyword Generator, Google's autocomplete, and the "People also ask" box.
fields: Primary keyword
The main phrase you want to rank for. Add monthly search volume and keyword difficulty (KD) if your tool shows them.
seo content brief (500 a month, KD 1)
Secondary keywords
Two or three related phrases the post should also cover.
seo content brief template, content brief template
Search intent
Why people search the primary keyword. Search it yourself and see what kind of page ranks.
Informational: step-by-step guides, most with a template
☐ Informational (learn)   ☐ Commercial (compare)   ☐ Transactional (buy)
Questions to answer
Questions from "People also ask" and autocomplete. These become headings and FAQs.
What is an SEO content brief? What should it include?

blocks.title: Competitor content (SERP analysis)
blocks.hint: The SERP is the search engine results page. Open the top three results that aren't ads and note what they cover and what they skip.
after: The AI summary at the top of the results. What it covers, and what it leaves out.

blocks.title: Content angle
fields: Content gap
What none of the top results do. Sum up section 03.
Every guide is written for agency teams, not people writing their own posts
Unique value
First-hand experience only you can add: a story, photo, result, or example from your own work.
My own filled-in brief and what I'd change
Editorial angle
The one idea your post adds, in one sentence.
A plain-language brief for people who write their own posts
Target word count
A range. Average the top three and divide by 3 for a starting point, not a rule.
900 to 1,200 words

blocks.title: On-page SEO
blocks.hint: What people see in Google before they click, and the address of the page.
fields: SEO title (title tag)
Primary keyword near the start. About 50 to 60 characters so Google doesn't cut it off.
How to Write an SEO Content Brief (With a Free Template)
Meta description
The summary under your title in Google. About 150 to 160 characters. Google may rewrite it.
How to write an SEO content brief in seven plain steps, what has changed in search and what hasn't, plus a free template you can download.
URL slug
The end of the web address. Short, lowercase, words separated by hyphens.
/blog/how-to-write-an-seo-content-brief

blocks.title: Ready to write?
blocks.body: You should be able to name the target audience, the search intent, and the content gap in one sentence each. If you can't, keep researching before you draft.

blocks.title: Content outline
blocks.hint: Your title is the H1. Big questions become H2 sections and follow-up questions become H3 subsections. A word count for each keeps the length on track.

1: Primary keyword in the first 100 words
8: Two or three questions from section 02
9: The call to action from section 08

blocks.title: Links, sources, and images
blocks.hint: Internal links go to your own posts. External links go to neutral sources, like the original report, not competitors. Use anchor text that says where the link goes. Credit every image.

blocks.title: Call to action and KPIs
fields: Call to action (CTA)
The one thing the reader should do after reading, plus the link.
Download the template
KPI (success metric)
One number that shows the post worked. Check it 30 days after publishing.
Template downloads and Google ranking for the primary keyword

blocks.title: Brand voice and guidelines
blocks.hint: Most useful when someone else is writing. If you write it yourself, use it to remember the rules you set.
fields: Brand voice and tone
How the post should sound.
Plain and friendly, first person
Must include
Required lines, disclaimers, product names, or terms.
A credit line for every image
Avoid
Claims, words, or topics to leave out.
Any number I can't link to a source

blocks.title: Pre-publish checklist
items: Primary keyword in the SEO title, the first 100 words, and one H2
SEO title and meta description match section 05
Every number links to a source you opened
Two or three internal links with clear anchor text
Images credited, each with alt text (a short description for screen readers)
The call to action matches the content goal in section 01
A calendar reminder to check your KPI in 30 days

example.title: Example: a filled-in brief
example.subtitle: The brief behind “Owala vs. Stanley: New Colors or New Products?” on angelphommachan.com. Search numbers from Ahrefs, US. Section word counts are from the finished post.
rows: Comparison, published on the angelphommachan.com blog (new post)
People starting out in marketing who want to see how two brands grow after one hit product
Readers understand the tradeoff between refreshing a best-seller and launching new products
owala vs stanley (1,800 searches a month, easy to rank for)
owala color drop (4,600), why is owala so popular (250), stanley marketing strategy
Commercial: shoppers comparing the bottles, so every top result is a product test
Is Owala more popular than Stanley? What is an Owala Color Drop?
No one compared the two brands’ marketing
My own side-by-side read of their products, ads, and blogs
New colors or new products: what each strategy costs and when it works
Average ÷ 3 ≈ 470 words; finished at about 1,480 to cover products, ads, and blogs
Owala vs. Stanley: New Colors or New Products?
Owala sells the same FreeSip in a new color every month. Stanley is building bags, coolers, and soccer collections around the Quencher. What each costs.
Notice where each brand’s ads and links send you, then answer: refresh it or build something new?
Google ranking for “owala vs stanley” and time on page after 30 days

Two bottles, two answers, plus a comparison table

Why Stanley is building past the Quencher
